title: A Bridge for the Uniform
premise: In 1919, in a snowbound river town on the edge of a former front, battlefield nurse Sebastian Almeida keeps a hidden ledger recording the soldiers the officers' reports erased — the deserters shot without trial, the wounded left to freeze, the dead listed as 'unfit for record.' When the seasonal bridge closes, trapping him with the very commandant whose signature fills those pages, Sebastian must decide whether fifteen years of careful silence were protection or complicity. With help from an unlikely found family — a disgraced chaplain, a telegraph operator who reads every message twice, and a widow who runs the checkpoint canteen — he smuggles the ledger out piece by piece before the thaw brings inspectors who will burn it. The book ends at the bridge itself: Sebastian surrenders himself so the final pages can cross, and the town, years later, carves the recovered names into the bridge's stone.
about_author: Edmund Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing military correspondence from the Great War and became obsessed with the gaps between official reports and soldiers' letters. He writes from a converted signal station on the northern coast, where the fog still arrives on schedule.

chapters.title: The Weight of Omitted Names
chapters.summary: Sebastian Almeida, now a quiet infirmary orderly in the river town of Vellmar, tends a dying veteran who murmurs names no report ever carried. That night Sebastian unlocks his old field ledger and adds three more. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: the ache of memory treated as contraband.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Practiced Silence
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter: young nurse Sebastian at the field hospital of Saint-Aubin, learning that speaking a forbidden name gets people transferred — or worse. He begins the ledger in a dead man's notebook. POV: Sebastian (1917). Emotional beat: the birth of deliberate invisibility.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: First frost seals Vellmar's bridge for the season; the garrison commandant, Colonel Hessler, announces winter checkpoints and martial order. Sebastian realizes the only road out is gone — and that Hessler has arrived asking questions about 'irregular records.' POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: claustrophobia disguised as routine.

chapters.title: The Widow at Checkpoint Two
chapters.summary: Marta Kellner runs the canteen at the second checkpoint, feeding soldiers and hearing everything. She recognizes Sebastian from Saint-Aubin though neither says so aloud. A wary alliance forms over coffee and unasked questions. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: two keepers of silence recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Chaplain Buried
chapters.summary: Father Anselm, defrocked for refusing to bless an execution, tends the garrison graveyard. He confesses to Sebastian that he kept his own record — a list of the men he buried unnamed. Together their documents corroborate. POV: Anselm. Emotional beat: guilt seeking purpose.

chapters.title: Hessler's Dinner Invitation
chapters.summary: The commandant invites Sebastian to dine, probing about the old field hospital with courteous menace; he suspects a ledger exists because a burned archive had missing pages. Sebastian lies well and hates how easily it comes. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: terror wearing a polite face.

chapters.title: The Telegraph Girl Reads Twice
chapters.summary: Ilse, the young telegraph operator, notices coded traffic ordering the destruction of remaining field records come spring. She brings the intercept to Sebastian, having guessed what he carries. The deadline becomes real: the thaw. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: a stranger choosing risk.

chapters.title: Ledger Arithmetic
chapters.summary: The four meet in the crypt beneath the chapel and count the ledger's sections against the checkpoints between them and the mainland post office. They devise a plan: split the evidence among trusted hands moving with legitimate winter shipments. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: fear converting into resolve.

chapters.title: A Name in the Canteen
chapters.summary: Marta discovers one ledger entry names her husband, executed as a deserter after the retreat — a death she was told was honorable. Grief nearly breaks the conspiracy when she wants to confront Hessler directly. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: love against duty, inverted.

chapters.title: The First Crossing Fails
chapters.summary: Ilse hides the first section in a medicine crate, but a random inspection at checkpoint one seizes the crate; the pages vanish into Hessler's office. The group must assume he now knows exactly what he's hunting. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: hope punctured, stakes doubled.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Hessler summons Sebastian again, lays the recovered pages on the table, and offers a bargain: the ledger for the town's safety, framed as mercy. Sebastian refuses without admitting ownership, and walks out expecting arrest that doesn't come. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: the strange power of not flinching.

chapters.title: Anselm's Bargain with God
chapters.summary: The chaplain volunteers to carry the largest section through checkpoint two inside the burial registry, arguing the dead have diplomatic immunity. He rehearses his own arrest like a liturgy. POV: Anselm. Emotional beat: faith repurposed as courage.

chapters.title: What Marta Saw in 1918
chapters.summary: Marta reveals she witnessed the executions her husband died in — she has been silent for her children's sake. Her testimony could hang Hessler, but only if she survives to give it. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: silence examined and found too expensive.

chapters.title: The Thaw Begins Early
chapters.summary: Unseasonable warmth cracks the river ice; inspectors will arrive within days, not weeks. Hessler orders the chapel crypt sealed for 'structural repair,' trapping the remaining ledger sections. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: time collapsing.

chapters.title: Breaking the Crypt
chapters.summary: The four retrieve the sections through the graveyard in a night operation, using a funeral as cover. Anselm is caught buying time for the others and taken without resistance, smiling. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: sacrifice made quietly, without spectacle.

chapters.title: The Cell Below
chapters.summary: Sebastian visits Anselm under pretext of last rites and learns Hessler hasn't found the ledger on him — but intends to trade the priest for it publicly. Sebastian must choose: save the man or the names. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: the theme sharpened to a single blade.

chapters.title: Ilse Rewires the Town
chapters.summary: Ilse cuts the garrison's telegraph line during a storm and sends the mainland post a false all-clear plus a request for immediate inspection, weaponizing Hessler's own bureaucracy against him. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: the smallest person landing the largest blow.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two, Last Light
chapters.summary: Marta walks the final ledger section across the bridge herself in a supply cart, passing her husband's executioner at arm's length, and hands it to the ferryman. She does not look back. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into delivery.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Dawn
chapters.summary: With the evidence away, Sebastian surrenders to Hessler at the bridge to buy the others amnesty, offering himself as the ledger's sole author. Hessler, facing imminent inspectors, accepts the trade. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: the invisible man making himself unmistakable.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: The inspectors arrive to find Hessler composed and Sebastian in irons — until the mainland post produces the ledger sections already received, timestamped and witnessed. Hessler is relieved of command on the ice he ordered swept. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: vindication arriving cold and procedural.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: In the chapel, Anselm freed, the town gathers while Sebastian reads the ledger's names aloud, including Marta's husband restored to honor. Some weep; some walk out; the record stands either way. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: memory returned to the community that owned it.

chapters.title: Stone and Season
chapters.summary: Years later, the reopened bridge bears carved names on its parapet. Sebastian, older, watches travelers cross without knowing what the stones cost, and finds that enough. Found family scattered but writing letters. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: quiet permanence after loud history.
